newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee steady vs fwd dlr, down in spot.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee steady vs fwd dlr, down in spot.

text.p: The Indian rupee was steady against the forward dollar but was down in the spot market in late morning trade on Wednesday, dealers said.
November-delivery dollars were quoted at a premium of 84/87 paise against Tuesday's close of 83/86.

"There has been some selling as well as buying of forward dollars in the morning but it is mainly interbank trade," said a dealer at a foreign bank. "Premiums are hardly changed from overnight levels."
"Any fresh move in premiums will take place tomorrow, depending on how call money reacts to today's bond auction," he said.
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) auctions 30 billion rupees of federal government bonds later on Wednesday.

"If call money hardens due to outflows towards the bond susbcriptions, we could see an uptick in forward premiums," the dealer said. "But it may not be much, a maximum of 3-4 paise for six-month dollars."
In the spot market, the rupee edged down to 35.84 per dollar on corporate month-end dollar demand, dealers said.
In latest deals, the rupee was quoted 35.832/842 per dollar after opening at 35.825/835. It closed Tuesday at 35.825/830.
"It appears to be month-end demand," said a dealer. "But dollar supply remains good and the downside for the rupee is limited....it may touch a maximum of 35.85."
"But if RBI also buys dollars, it may dip further," he said.
